title: Text encoders: CLIP, T5 and LLM encoders
hook: What each encoder gives the model and what it costs. CLIP in ComfyUI is causal, T5 isn't, and neither of them hands over only the last token.

verified.claim: CLIPTextModel_ adds a causal mask (triu of the scores) before its encoder.
T5Stack builds a mask only from padding, so a token can attend to tokens after it.
Llama2_ adds a causal mask when the sequence is longer than one token, outside one decode path.
CLIP's pooled vector is taken at the end token, and the tensor keeps every token's row.
SD 1.5 and SDXL settings: 77 per chunk, widths 768 and 1280, layer choices.
Klein reads layers 9, 18 and 27 of Qwen3 and stacks them, with a minimum length of 512, a chat template and weights off.
Chunk and shape arithmetic in the lab, and the mask experiment, on random numbers.
Paper titles and the abstracts of CLIP and T5.

unchecked: We did not load any real text encoder for this lesson, so nothing here measures a real prompt or quality.
We don't claim that one encoder gives better pictures. That depends on the whole model, which was trained with its encoder.
The draft said T5 handles long prompts better. We did not test that, and removed it as a quality claim. What we can state is that T5 has no 77-token chunking.
We did not read every LLM encoder in core. Others may pick different layers.
